explanation: Fires on the main verb that comes directly after a sentence-initial singular person subject (a surname, first name or 'She'/'He'), as in 'Spence said', 'Kypri says', 'Smith explains/argues/asserts/believes'. It peaks at about 0.8-1.0 x max for speech and cognition verbs and reaches about 0.55-0.7 for other verbs ('walked', 'eats'). It is weaker (about 0.45) when the subject is plural or not a person ('They said', 'The data said'), when the verb comes after a quote ('"It failed," Smith said'), or when the name is a possessive ('Smith's report'). A secondary job: the infix ' +' in 'Let w be o/4 + 2 + ...' arithmetic reaches about 1.0. Inactive class (measured peak below 0.25 x max): texts of 10-50 tokens made only of integers separated by commas, spaces or hyphens (0.10-0.23), and plain URLs of 15-25 tokens with no word-like file names (0.09-0.14). Outside the inactive class: ordinary English prose with no person-subject + verb (the background there is 0.26-0.53 x max, so it is not inactive), decimal lists (0.28), CJK text (0.57) and code or arithmetic with '+'.
